significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish a form-(iii) predictive law: the per-fact "minimal ablation-set size = redundancy" increases with factual robustness and predicts both "edit-resistance" and "noise tolerance," while also supporting a causal mechanism in which several independent MLP loci can each sustain recall. This would constrain expectations across multiple outcomes—not merely locate knowledge—by predicting which facts will survive ablation, recover under paraphrased post-edit queries, and tolerate activation noise; that bears directly on the localization assumptions used in ROME (Meng et al., 2022), MEMIT (Meng et al., 2023), and examined critically by Hase et al.'s "Does Localization Inform Editing?" (2023). The phenomenon and mechanism are both determinate, and a verified-false result would informatively reject redundancy count as the common explanation connecting recall robustness, editing resistance, and noise tolerance, rather than merely report failure to find a locus. Topic-substitution check: replacing these linked, quantitative predictions with the generic topic of knowledge organization would not earn this score; the graded per-fact coupling is specific and substantially more constraining than the topic's obvious localized-versus-distributed hypothesis.

reach.justification: The transferable handle is the explicitly named "redundancy count" or "minimal ablation-set size," proposed as a diagnostic for "which facts are safely editable and which will resist editing." It is ex ante with respect to an attempted edit or noise-induced failure, providing model editors an action window to select methods or flag likely resistant facts, although obtaining it requires interventions rather than a lightweight deployment-time probe. After per-model re-extraction, the substantive prediction survives as a relation—higher redundancy should forecast edit resistance and noise robustness—rather than offering only an uncommitted procedure for searching for loci; the asserted scope is "across models and a large fact set," with uptake by knowledge-editing and model-auditing practitioners. Topic-substitution check: the broad knowledge-retrieval topic alone supplies neither this predictor nor its lead time, so the score rests on the claim-specific diagnostic, though the absence of an asserted cross-architecture or outside-AI design rule keeps its reach below the top band.
